results.title: Dance in the primary school
results.creator_credit: Derek Monk, Freelance Directors and Schools Council
results.brief_description: Shows what can be achieved with children of different ages and varying ability and experience. Illustrates the framework of a lesson; some stimuli used to initiate movement - voice, percussion, pictures; how several teachers, drawing on their own resources enrich the children’s experience; ways to extend children in the main part of the lesson; development of a simple group dance.

results.title: Dance Dans Tanz Danse
results.brief_description: Founded in 1926 by Marie Rambert, Rambert Dance Company is one of dance’s most consistently innovative and imaginative companies. Here are three modern dances by the company featuring music by Bill Withers. The three are: “Lonely Town, Lonely Street” a jazz ballet which conveys a picture of lonely people in a large city; “Intimate Pages” using Janacek’s Second String Quartet; and “Sergeant Early’s Dream” recalling the folklore of the old world with British, Irish and American folk songs. Rated: G

results.title: Damsels be damned
results.brief_description: A fantastic fairytale, with the ambivalence and logic of a dream. Deals with the difference between the fairy tale stereotype of women as beautiful princesses awaiting their prince charmings and the real world of male and female relationships. “Damsels Be Damned” entwines fantasy, fiction and reality. Offbeat and amusing it plunges below the surface of sexual stereotypes to the darkness of sexual assault.

results.title: Damned whores and evil bitches: prostitution in Australia 1788-1988
results.creator_credit: Rosa Colosimo and Rosa Colosimo Productions
results.brief_description: Australia’s founding mothers arrived in 1788 and their legacy continues to thrive as a multi million dollar industry. A revealing expose of prostitution, the oldest profession, from colonial to modern times and its impact on Australian society through dramatic re-enactments, archival material, contemporary footage and interviews. Narrated by Tracy Harvey.
